tags.chapter_name: Center of Mass Momentum and Collision

question.text: Two particles of masses <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi mathvariant="normal">m</mi></math> and <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>3</mn><mi mathvariant="normal">m</mi></math> approach each other with different velocities. After collision, the particle of mass <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi mathvariant="normal">m</mi></math> has velocity <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mover><mi>v</mi><mo>→</mo></mover></math> in their centre of mass frame. Velocity of particle of mass <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>3</mn><mi mathvariant="normal">m</mi></math> in the centre of mass frame is

solution.text:
In the centre of mass frame, the total linear momentum of the  system is zero.

Hence, mv→+3mv→'=0

or v→'=-v→3
